Inglewood, California
  August 20, 2019

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on
Tuesday, August 20, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into session for Closed Session at the hour of
1:01 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for Closed Session were as follows:

  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor
Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on the Closed Session Item.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session
Item No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called
the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing
Authority, Finance Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:04 p.m.
The City Clerk/ Successor Agency Secretary/  Housing Authority
Secretary/Finance Authority Secretary/Joint Powers  Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority  Chairman/Finance  Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council  Members/Successor  Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members/Finance
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Joint Powers
Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk/Acting Secretary*
Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
Jeffrey Lewis  Sr. Assistant City Attorney/Sr. Assistant General Counsel*
David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
Cheryl Moore  Management Assistant

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  1
 August 20, 2019

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded
  by Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member
  Dotson that the demands presented to the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority dated, August 16, 2019, in the amount of
  $10,448,268.20, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  131.8  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 19-16 INTRODUCED
  AND ADOPTED - EXTENDING THE MORATORIUM AN ADDITIONAL
  10 MONTHS AND 15 DAYS ON ANY SELF-STORAGE FACILITIES. The
  City Clerk announced that the next scheduled matter is a public hearing to
  consider adopting an Ordinance extending the moratorium an additional 10
  months and 15 days on any self-storage facilities in the City of Inglewood
  established by Ordinance No. 19-15, that notice was given in the time, form, and
  manner as required by law, and that no communication was received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated August 20, 2019.

  Christopher Jackson, Director of Economic and Community Development, gave a
  brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the
  City Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded
  by Council Member Dotson that the City Council does hereby receive, file and
  accept the report describing the measurers taken to alleviate the condition(s)
  which prompted the adoption of Emergency Ordinance No. 19-15 that established
  a 45-day moratorium. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor
  Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Mayor Butts that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor
  Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  Furthermore, Ordinance No. 19-16 entitled:

  EXTENSION OF URGENCY INTERIM ORDINANCE NO. 19-15
  FOR AN ADDITIONAL 10 MONTHS AND 15 DAYS,
  ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON ANY AND ALL

  2
 August 20, 2019

  BUILDING PERMITS, BUSINESS PERMITS, CONDITIONAL
  USE  PERMITS,  OR  ANY  ENTITLEMENTS  FOR
  ESTABLISHING OR EXPANDING ANY SELF-STORAGE
  FACILITY ANYWHERE IN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD

  was introduced by Council Member Franklin.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Mayor
  Butts that Ordinance No. 19-16 entitled:

  EXTENSION OF URGENCY INTERIM ORDINANCE NO. 19-15
  FOR AN ADDITIONAL 10 MONTHS AND 15 DAYS,
  ESTABLISHING A MORATORIUM ON ANY AND ALL
  BUILDING PERMITS, BUSINESS PERMITS, CONDITIONAL
  USE  PERMITS,  OR  ANY  ENTITLEMENTS  FOR
  ESTABLISHING OR EXPANDING ANY SELF-STORAGE
  FACILITY ANYWHERE IN THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor
  Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

  132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending
  specific actions be taken on various claim filings.

  Reject the following claims in accordance with Government Code Section 913:
  Letters from the City Attorney’s Office recommending specific actions be taken
  on various claim filings.

  a) Stacey Meadors for alleged personal injury on March 27, 2019.
  b) Farmers Insurance subro Armando Navarro dba Melo Burgers for alleged
  loss of business income on February 26, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member
  Dotson, and carried that the above listed claims be denied.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on July 23,
  2019, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 101  AGREEMENT NO. 19-271 APPROVED – LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL CONTROL. Staff report dated August 20,
  2019, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with Los Angeles
  County Department of Animal Care and Control to provide the City with animal
  care and control services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-271 in the
  annual amount of $275,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 142  AGREEMENT NO. 16-064 APPROVED – LANCE SOLL & LUNGHARD
  LLP (LSL). Staff report dated August 20, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval to exercise the option to renew Agreement No. 16-064 with Lance Soll
  & Lunghard LLP (LSL) for an additional year to provide audit services.

  3
 August 20, 2019

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve renewal Agreement No. 16-064 in
  the amount of $127,206. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 173  AGREEMENT NO. 19-272 APPROVED – SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE
  INVESTMENT BOARD, INC. Staff report dated August 20, 2019, was
  presented recommending approval of non-financial Work Experience Agreements
  with the South Bay Workforce Investment Board, Inc.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-272 with
  the South Bay Workforce Investment Board, Inc. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 156  PURCHASE APPROVED - CISCO CATALYST 9600 SERIES NETWORK
  SWITCH AND COMPONENTS. Staff report dated August 20, 2019, was
  presented recommending approval to purchase a Cisco Catalyst 9600 Series
  Network Switch and components from Logicalis, Inc.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve the purchase in the amount of
  $158,899.22. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 183  PAYMENT APPROVED – BRADEN CONSULTING. Staff report dated
  August 20, 2019, was presented recommending approval of a one-time payment
  to Braden Consulting for professional management services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby approve payments in the amount of
  $12,915. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

 178  GRANT FUNDS ACCEPTED – FISCAL YEAR 2019 JUSTICE
  ASSISTANCE GRANT FUNDS. Staff report dated August 20, 2019, was
  presented recommending the acceptance of the Fiscal Year 2019 Justice
  Assistance Grant Funds.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Receive and file the report
  pertaining to the United States Department of Justice (USDOJ) FY 2019 Byrne
  Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG); 2) Accept and approve the
  recommendation of the Chief of Police pertaining to the expenditure of FY 2019
  JAG funds; 3) Approve Certifications and Assurances required for the acceptance
  of FY 2019 JAG funds; and 4) Authorize the expenditure of FY 2019 JAG funds
  in the amount of $55,981 for the approved recommendation, and direct that funds
  be included in the 2019 – 2020 fiscal year budget. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  4
 August 20, 2019

103.3  PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING INVOICE APPROVED – KARABUILD

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  ANNUAL BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  103.3  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 19-274 APPROVED –
  HHJ CONSTRUCTION, INC.; RESOLUTION NO. 19-104 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019 BUDGET. Staff report dated
  August 20, 2019, was presented recommending award of contract and approval of
  an agreement with HHJ Construction, Inc., to provide residential sound insulation
  work on 58 residential units (RSI Phase XV, Group 22), per Bid No. CB-19-10.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve
  Agreement No. 19-274 in the amount of $1,946.483 (includes a 10% contingency
  in the amount of $176,953: 2) Approve special expenses in the amount of
  $58,464; and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 19-104 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2018/2019
  ANNUAL BUDGET

  5
 August 20, 2019

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts;
  and
  Noes: None.

  131.8  AGREEMENT NO. 19-275 APPROVED – COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES;
  HOMELESS PLAN APPROVED; RESOLUTION NO. 19-105 ADOPTED –
  ACCEPTING THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGLES HOMELESS
  INITIATIVE – MEASURE H CITIES HOMELESS IMPLEMENTATION
  GRANT AND AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2018-2019 BUDGET.
  Staff report dated August 20, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an
  agreement with the County of Los Angeles for the Homeless Initiative – Measure
  H Cities Implementation Grant.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Dotson that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve the City of Inglewood
  Homeless Plan; 2) Approve Agreement No. 19-275 in the amount of $105,000;
  and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 19-105 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING THE CITY’S PLAN TO

  COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES TO IMPLEMENT THE CITY’S

 132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
